headline: Profitability returns as double-digit growth continues
summary_short: Bill.com's fiscal Q3 2026 revenue rose 13.5% y/y to $406.6M (down 2.0% q/q), while net income swung to $12.8M from losses of $2.6M last quarter and $11.6M a year ago, lifting diluted EPS to $0.12.
summary_long: Revenue rose 13.5% y/y to $406.6M, driven by higher transaction fees on a 12% y/y rise in total payment volume ($88.7B) and subscription growth, partly offset by lower interest income on customer funds. Gross margin expanded to 81.6% from 81.2% on lower personnel costs. Net income swung to $12.8M (diluted EPS $0.12) from losses in both the prior quarter and year-ago quarter, aided by R&D savings from software capitalization and workforce reductions, partially offset by higher card-rewards expense in sales and marketing. Cash fell 5.1% y/y to $994.7M as the company continued its share buyback program. No forward guidance appears in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Grew on a $44.5M increase in transaction fees from higher payment volume and customer adoption, plus a $6.3M rise in subscription fees, partly offset by a $2.5M drop in interest income on customer funds from lower rates.
Gross margin expanded to 81.6% from 81.2% primarily due to lower personnel-related costs, including stock-based compensation, charged to cost of revenue.

Swing to profit driven by revenue growth, R&D savings from higher software capitalization, and RIF-driven personnel savings, partly offset by higher card-rewards expense and restructuring charges from the RIFs.
Reflects the net income swing to profit; diluted share count also rose 12.1% q/q as dilutive equity awards became includable once the company returned to profitability.
Service costs rose y/y on higher direct transaction-processing and data-hosting costs from increased customer adoption, and higher amortization of capitalized internal-use software.

Operating loss narrowed as revenue growth outpaced expenses; R&D fell on higher capitalized software costs and RIF-driven savings, partly offset by restructuring charges and higher card-rewards expense.

Management cited reductions in force (October 2025, March 2026, and a planned up-to-30% RIF announced in May 2026) alongside continued investment in AI agents as it pursues greater operating efficiency and profitability.
